before: The writing master asks who touched his ink. You raise a perfectly black finger to deny it.
after: You practise your letters on a broken roof tile. The first good letter is so large that there is no room for the rest of your name.

before: The other children elect you shepherd of a flock of stones. None stray. Your reputation for husbandry is impeccable.
after: You herd a flock of stones across the yard. They are obedient sheep until someone tries to put one in a pocket.

before: You build a snow lord with an enormous nose. The thaw removes his authority before anyone can collect rent.
after: Your snowman has the reeve’s enormous nose. When the reeve comes past, you hastily add a moustache.

before: A merchant overpaid you by mistake and rode off. You said nothing. Wise.
after: A merchant counts out six gold too many and rides away. You close your purse before anyone asks you to check it.

before: You slip beside the watering trough. A bystander offers advice after you have stopped needing it.
after: You slip beside the watering trough and come up with duckweed in your hair. A bystander turns away to cough very noisily into a sleeve.

before: {{carer}} marks your height on the doorpost. You are now taller than last year’s debt notice.
after: {{carer}} marks your height on the doorpost. You stand on tiptoe and wait to see whether it counts.

before: You discover that dropping a spoon makes an adult fetch it. An excellent arrangement, briefly.
after: You try to fit an enormous bite into your mouth. Half reaches your chin. You pat it back up with both hands.

before: During the sickness scare you avoid the crowded stalls. You miss the company more than the haggling.
after: You catch a rough cough during the market sickness scare. Several nights pass without good sleep; even the haggling outside sounds distant.
